enchanted_outlines.config.title: Enchanted Outlines
enchanted_outlines.config.subtitle: Colored outlines for enchanted items
enchanted_outlines.config.enable.tooltip: Master switch. When off, no outline is rendered anywhere.
enchanted_outlines.config.thickness.tool: How many pixels the outline expands beyond the item sprite (GUI / held items / projectiles). Decimal values are allowed. 0 disables the expansion.
enchanted_outlines.config.armorThickness: How many pixels the outline expands beyond the worn armor model. Decimal values are allowed. 0 disables the expansion.
enchanted_outlines.config.itemPixelColor: Shader-compat mode only (with shaders off, outlines are always pure color): when ON, the outline color is mixed with each item pixel color (applies to flat and 3D items; keeps the item silhouette; the mixed colors look unique). When OFF, the outline is a pure color — flat items still keep their silhouette (reads texture alpha; one-time cost on first render), 3D items keep their geometry-driven shape. Shield/trident box models are always pure color.
enchanted_outlines.config.armorPixelColo: Shader-compat mode only (with shaders off, outlines are always pure color): when ON, armor/elytra/projectile outlines sample the original texture alpha mask (hug the layered texture silhouette; color mixes with the texture). When OFF, the outline is a pure color (shape follows the model geometry).
enchanted_outlines.config.outlineExposur: Shader-compat mode only, applies when color mixing is OFF: the pure-color outline is darkened by the item texture's average brightness (dark items like iron swords get much dimmer outlines, bright items stay bright), mimicking how the mix mode lowers exposure by the item color — hue is preserved. When OFF, pure-color outlines keep their full brightness.
enchanted_outlines.config.sodiumAnimated: Sodium's animate-only-visible-textures optimization freezes animated textures of enchanted items (its visibility tracking does not cover the enchanted render path). When ON, this mod marks enchanted item sprites active via Sodium's public API at item render entry points, keeping the optimization while exempting enchanted items (default). When OFF, no marking is done (if freezing reappears, disable Sodium's animate-only-visible-textures manually). No effect without Sodium installed.
enchanted_outlines.config.bewlr3dScale.t: Outline inflate scale for modded custom-model weapons (BEWLR, e.g. crescent spear / Cataclysm weapons). The 3D expansion is thickness x scale x distance-to-center (whole-box) or a fixed offset (per-cube); slender weapons need a larger base scale to look visible.
enchanted_outlines.config.bewlr3dPerCube: true = per-cube vertex-normal expansion (uniform thickness, no tip inflation on slender weapons; recommended). false = whole bounding-box inflation (old algorithm, tips expand more).
enchanted_outlines.config.bewlrCaptureV2: Capture-based outline algorithm v2 (normalized capture, 2026-09-25): captures the mod renderer's output with an identity PoseStack, yielding geometry in the renderer's own model space (independent of camera/GUI pixel space). Guards apply uniformly to every context (junk geometry is always rejected, curing the giant-model bug), outline thickness matches the pixel semantics of the standard GUI/held paths, and position replays through the real pose matrix for 100% body alignment. Renderers that require a real pose fall back to the v1 algorithm automatically. false = v1 legacy algorithm (pose-copied capture, center-distance guard on held contexts only).
enchanted_outlines.config.bewlrGlobalBuf: ON by default (2026-09-26 v1-bypass redesign): some renderers (TACZ BedrockModel.render) bypass the passed buffer and write straight into the global shared bufferSource, so plain capture gets no geometry. When ON, the global bufferSource is temporarily swapped during capture and the capture runs with the REAL pose — captured vertices equal the body's final draw coordinates, emitted raw with zero replay. The old v2.1 identity+replay combination produced assumed-space garbage for pose-reading renderers (root cause of the giant-misplacement regression) and has been removed. Capture statistics are throttled-logged (swap-stats); if misalignment appears, turn this off to return to no-outline.
enchanted_outlines.config.hazenCompat.to: Enables outlines for Hazen'N Stuff (hazennstuff:) BEWLR/Geo weapons (e.g. Starfury and other GeckoLib models). It first samples the body texture alpha for the silhouette (flat parts never inflate into a solid plane), then falls back to render-capture, covering all Hazen weapon model types. When off, these weapons get no outline. Flat items and AzureLib armor are unaffected.
enchanted_outlines.config.taczCompat.too: Enables outlines for TACZ guns (tacz:). World contexts (first/third person, dropped, item frames) are outlined by a walk-through mixin injected inside TaCZ (BedrockGunModel.render HEAD), synced with animations/aiming/LOD; GUI (slot flat plane) uses flat capture. If a pose still misbehaves, turn this off to return to no-outline. Flat items and AzureLib armor are unaffected.
enchanted_outlines.config.taczFirstPerso: First-person TACZ gun outline ring width = base thickness x this multiplier, default 2.0 (first-person rings looked thin in playtesting). Adjust between 0.5 and 4.0; 1.0 matches third-person/dropped width.
enchanted_outlines.config.armorUniformEx: true = every armor part (cube) expands by a fixed thickness, so modded fine-grained models (e.g. thermal springstone armor) get outlines as thick as vanilla armor. false = scale proportional to part size (old algorithm; small parts get thinner outlines).
enchanted_outlines.config.mergeMode.tool: When an item has several enchantments, which color wins?
enchanted_outlines.config.defaultColor.t: Hex RGB (RRGGBB) used for enchantments that have no specific color mapped. The outline is fully opaque.
Comma-separated map: id=RRGGBB. e.g. minecraft:sharpness=FFD700,minecraft:fire_aspect=FF6A00. Uses the default color when an enchantment is not listed.
enchanted_outlines.config.itemColors.too: Comma-separated map: itemid=RRGGBB. Overrides the enchantment color for that item; modded item ids work directly.
enchanted_outlines.config.enabledItems.t: Comma-separated item ids that may get an outline; empty = all items (default). Supports wildcards: minecraft:* matches the whole minecraft namespace, minecraft:di* matches ids starting with di. The blacklist (disabledItems) is applied after the whitelist.
Comma-separated item ids that never get an outline, even when enchanted. Supports wildcards: minecraft:* disables the whole minecraft namespace.
enchanted_outlines.config.itemThicknesse: Per-item outline thickness: itemid=pixels, comma separated; overrides the global thickness (modded items work directly). Programmatic registration (OutlineColorRegistry.registerItemThickness) takes precedence over this. Example: 'minecraft:diamond_sword=2.5,tacz:modern_kinetic_gun=1.5'.
enchanted_outlines.config.solidColorItem: Items whose outline is ALWAYS pure color, even in shader-compat mode with mixing on. Comma separated; supports wildcards: minecraft:* matches a whole namespace. With shaders off all outlines are pure color anyway, so this list only matters in shader mode.
enchanted_outlines.config.bewlrNamespace: Namespace-to-adapter registry: namespace=kind, comma separated. Kinds: capture = capture-first (default, outline follows animation); legacy = reflection/Geo direct first (old behavior); off = no outline for that namespace. Unconfigured namespaces use the default capture-first chain — when a new mod misbehaves, change the config instead of waiting for a code fix. Stacks with the TACZ/Hazen compat toggles. Example: hazennstuff=legacy,somemod=off
enchanted_outlines.config.enableRPGRainb: Enable RPG rainbow effect (dynamic rainbow outlines): true = outline color changes over time, forming a rainbow effect (highest priority, overrides all other color configs); false = use normal color config.
